(a) ERISA Amendments.—
        (1) PBGC recipients.—Section 602(2)(A)(v) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (29 U.S.C. 
1162(2)(A)(v)) is amended by striking “December 31, 2010” and inserting “February 12, 2011”. 
        (2) TAA-eligible individuals.—Section 602(2)(A)(vi) of such Act (29 U.S.C. 1162(2)(A)(vi)) is amended by striking “December 31, 2010” and inserting “February 12, 2011”.  
    (b) IRC Amendments.—
        (1) PBGC recipients.—Section 4980B(f)(2)(B)(i)(V) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking “December 31, 2010” and inserting “February 12, 2011”. 
        (2) TAA-eligible individuals.—Section 4980B(f)(2)(B)(i)(VI) of such Code is amended by striking “December 31, 2010” and inserting “February 12, 2011”.  
    (c) PHSA Amendments.—Section 2202(2)(A)(iv) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 300bb–2(2)(A)(iv)) is amended by striking “December 31, 2010” and inserting “February 12, 2011”. 
    (d) Effective Date.—The amendments made by this section shall apply to periods of coverage which would (without regard to the amendments made by this section) end on or after December 31, 2010.

fable.w: This section only makes technical date changes to ERISA, the Internal Revenue Code, and the Public Health Service Act, extending COBRA continuation coverage periods for PBGC recipients and TAA-eligible individuals. The tempting reading is that because it affects private individuals and plans, outsiders are involved, but nothing here has the federal government consulting, hearing from, or being sued by any outside party. There is no rulemaking, comment period, advisory body, or consultation.
fable.s: is amended by striking “December 31, 2010” and inserting “February 12, 2011”

opus.w: This section only replaces "December 31, 2010" with "February 12, 2011" in ERISA, the Internal Revenue Code and the Public Health Service Act, and sets an effective date. No outside party is consulted on, or given a way to challenge, any federal decision. The references to PBGC recipients and TAA-eligible individuals only describe who gets the extended benefit, and benefit eligibility does not count as participation.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "PBGC recipients" and "TAA-eligible individuals" refer to outside people dealing with federal programs. That fails the definition: these provisions only change the dates on which continuation health coverage ends. They create no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to statutory dates in various acts (ERISA, IRC, PHSA). It does not create any mechanism for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The changes are legislative directives regarding effective dates, not participatory processes.
qwen_chat.s: (a) ERISA Amendments.— (1) PBGC recipients.—Section 602(2)(A)(v) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (29 U.S.C. 1162(2)(A)(v)) is amended by striking “December 31, 2010” and inserting “February 12, 2011”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing dates for benefit eligibility involves public participation because it affects individuals. However, the text itself only describes statutory amendments to dates and effective dates; it does not establish any process for the public to consult, comment, or participate in the decision-making. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits, and this section is merely a technical amendment to existing law, not a procedural requirement for participation.
